title: Epochal KV migration and prefill safety layers for paged-attention
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce an epochal migration mechanism that safely relocates fragmented KV slots across slab/stripe boundaries while coordinating a two-phase prefill safety layer to ensure no decode regressions or tail-latency spikes during migration. The feature targets long-lived tenants that observe increasing fragmentation and decode stalls caused by opportunistic evictions and non-deterministic kernel handoffs.
background: We have recurring incidents where KV fragmentation and cross-shard slot churn cause prefill misses and transient decode tail spikes for long-sequence workloads. Current eviction heuristics attempt to reclaim by touch-frequency alone, which leads to repeated re-population of small fragments and suboptimal kernel selection because prefill windows see high miss rates.
proposed_solution: 1) Add an epoch tag to KV reservations and a migration controller that batches candidate slots into migration epochs. 2) Implement a staged demotion: candidate slots are first soft-demoted (lower residency score, still readable) then epoch-migrated into contiguous stripes during low-util windows. 3) Introduce a Prefill Safety Layer that: a) records prefill intent for migrating prefixes, b) pins required KV entries for active prefill windows, and c) signals kernel scheduler to prefer compacted kernel variants for pinned ranges. 4) Expose an opt-in runtime flag per-tenant to enable conservative vs aggressive migration profiles.
design_decisions: Use epoch-based coordination instead of immediate in-place compaction to avoid long lock holds on hot slabs
Two-phase demotion ensures reads still succeed during migration and reduces mid-decode cache thrash
Prefill safety pins are time-bounded to prevent permanent hot-residency abuse
Kernel hinting will be advisory; kernels can ignore hints under emergency fallback to maintain availability
tasks: Spec: finalise epoch lifecycle, demotion timeouts, and migration window heuristics (owner: Maya)
Runtime: implement epoch tag on slot metadata and migration controller (owner: Liam)
Prefill: add prefill intent API and pin/unpin logic; integrate with admission controller (owner: Priya Rao)
Kernel: add hint channel for compact-kernel preference and fallbacks (owner: Kenji Sato)
Tests: unit tests for migration controller, integration tests with streaming decode under load (owner: QA)
Telemetry: add metrics for migration epochs, pinned-slot counts, prefill-hit-rate delta (owner: Observability)
Docs: runtime config docs and migration safety guide (owner: Docs)
PRs: create incremental PRs scoped to epoch tag, migration controller, and prefill safety integration
acceptance_criteria: No user-visible 5xx or decode corruption introduced by migration in canary cluster
Prefill-hit-rate on long-sequence synthetic workload increases by >= 12% compared to baseline when enabled
95th-percentile decode-latency does not regress more than 5% during steady-state migration windows
Telemetry surfaces epoch transitions, and pinned-slot counts are bounded by configured limits
Opt-in flag successfully toggles conservative/aggressive behavior without restart
test_plan: Synthetic benchmark: run 10k long-context requests with fragmentation pattern A and compare prefill hit-rate baseline vs epochal migration enabled
Chaos test: induce slab pressure and validate pinned slots release within timeout
Canary rollout: enable for single tenant in staging region for 48h with debug logging
Kernel compatibility: validate compact-kernel hint path on A100 and T4 variants using microbench harness
Regression: run full CI with streaming decode and KV stress harness
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime flag and tenant opt-in
Stage 1: Enable in internal staging with conservative profile for 48h
Stage 2: Canary on a low-traffic customer with aggressive profile for 72h
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to broader population with telemetry gates every 6h
Rollback: flag-off and immediate unpin/unmigrate sweep if prefill-hit-rate drops > 8% or 5xx increases

notes: Risk: aggressive migration may temporarily increase memory copy bandwidth; observe GPU PCIe contention during canary
Trade-off: conservative profile favours stability over fragmentation reduction; aggressive profile favours reclamation speed
Future: consider cross-tenant cooperative migration for underutilized slabs if multi-tenancy telemetry indicates benefit
